text:
Over recent decades, many young families have left villages for cities, where there are more jobs and better schools. This has raised incomes and given children more opportunities. But the villages they left are emptying: schools and shops are closing, the older residents who remain are increasingly isolated, and local councils are spending more and more on transport and home visits to support them.
Which one of the following could be drawn as a conclusion of the above passage?
options: The gains from families moving to cities have to be weighed against the costs to the people left behind and to councils.
Older villagers expect councils, not their families, to look after them.
Families should stay in their home villages.
Councils should pay for transport so that families are free to move.
Families should put their elderly relatives before their careers.
solution: The passage gives benefits of moving (incomes, opportunities) and costs (isolated older people, rising council spending), so the fair conclusion is that the two must be weighed. It does not say what older people expect, and it does not recommend staying, paying for transport or putting relatives first.

text:
The government plans to require that the source code of any software used to run public services be published. Supporters say citizens have a right to know how these systems make decisions. But software firms fear that rivals will copy code they have spent years developing. Therefore, through fear of imitators, software firms will stop bidding for public contracts.
Which one of the following, if true, would most weaken this argument?
options: There are already enough software systems for public services.
Copyright law forbids rivals from using published code in their own products.
The software industry is highly competitive.
Citizens may trust public services less once they can read the code.
Other countries already publish the code of their public-service software.
solution: The argument depends on publication letting rivals copy the code. If copyright law forbids that, the firms' fear has little basis and they need not stop bidding. A competitive industry makes the fear stronger; the number of systems already in use, citizens' trust and other countries' practice do not address whether copying is possible.

text: In which modern country was the centre of the Aztec Empire?
solution: The Aztec capital, Tenochtitlan, was built on a lake island where Mexico City now stands; it fell to Hernán Cortés in 1521. The Inca Empire was centred in Peru, and the Maya lived across southern Mexico and Guatemala.

text: In medical research, a "double-blind" trial is one in which
options: patients are not told what illness they have.
two different drugs are tested at the same time.
the whole trial is run twice.
neither the patients nor the researchers treating them know who is receiving the real treatment.
the results are checked by two separate teams.
solution: In a double-blind trial, neither the patients nor the people giving the treatment know who has the real treatment and who has a placebo, so expectations cannot bias the results. In a single-blind trial only the patients are unaware.

text: Which general crossed the river Rubicon with his army in 49 BC, starting a civil war in the Roman Republic?
solution: Julius Caesar led his army across the Rubicon, the boundary of his province, which by law he could not do under arms; "crossing the Rubicon" still means taking a step with no way back. Pompey was his rival in the war that followed, and Hannibal and Scipio fought each other in the Second Punic War.

text: In which city is the headquarters of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)?
solution: The FAO, which leads international efforts against hunger, has its headquarters in Rome. Geneva hosts the WHO, New York the UN General Assembly, Vienna the International Atomic Energy Agency, and Paris UNESCO.

text:
A cinema has six screens. Four of them have 12 rows of 15 seats; the other two have 8 rows of 12 seats.
Online sales stop as soon as 75% of all the seats in the cinema are taken. Ten seats are reserved for staff, who always use them, and these count towards the 75% but are never sold online.
What is the largest number of tickets that can be sold online?
solution: Seats: 4 x 12 x 15 = 720 and 2 x 8 x 12 = 192, so 912 in all. 75% of 912 is 684 seats, but 10 of those are staff seats, leaving 674 for online sales. 684 forgets the staff seats; 902 subtracts them from the whole cinema instead of from the 75%.

text:
A small box of tea contains 80 g and costs €3.20. A large box contains 125 g and costs €4.50.
Working in euros per kilogram, how much cheaper is the tea in the large box?
solution: Small box: €3.20 for 0.08 kg is €40 per kg. Large box: €4.50 for 0.125 kg is €36 per kg. The large box is €4.00 per kg cheaper. The difference in box prices (€1.30) says nothing about value, because the boxes hold different amounts.

text:
A club of 600 members elects a president, one vote per member. If no candidate wins more than half of the votes cast in the first round, the top two go through to a second round. In the first round, one candidate received 180 votes, and a second round was held.
Which one of the following describes what is possible for this candidate?
options: The candidate must have won the election.
The candidate must have been in the second round.
The candidate cannot have won the election.
The candidate may have won, may have come second, or may have been knocked out in the first round.
The candidate must have been knocked out in the first round.
solution: Up to 420 other votes were shared among the rival candidates. They could have split into two totals above 180 (for example 210 and 210), knocking the candidate out in third place. Or they could have split among several candidates below 180 (for example 170, 160 and 90), making the candidate first and putting them in a second round they might win or lose. So all three outcomes are possible.

text:
The table shows the winning height in the high jump at a championship held every two years. A new record is set only when the height beats every earlier winning height.

| year | height (m) | year | height (m) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2000 | 2.20 | 2012 | 2.29 |
| 2002 | 2.25 | 2014 | 2.27 |
| 2004 | 2.22 | 2016 | 2.31 |
| 2006 | 2.24 | 2018 | 2.33 |
| 2008 | 2.30 | 2020 | 2.32 |
| 2010 | 2.28 | | |

What is the longest time for which a championship record stood unbroken?
solution: Records: 2.20 (2000), broken in 2002 by 2.25; that stood until 2008 (6 years), when 2.30 was set; 2.30 stood until 2016 (8 years), when 2.31 was set; 2.31 was beaten by 2.33 in 2018. The longest spell is 8 years, from 2008 to 2016. Heights such as 2.29 in 2012 were good but did not beat the record.

text:
A bottle of dishwasher gel says it holds enough for 30 washes, using one full cap of gel for each wash. I find that two-thirds of a cap is enough.
How many washes will I get from the bottle?
solution: The bottle holds 30 full caps. Each wash uses two-thirds of a cap, so the number of washes is 30 / (2/3) = 30 x 3/2 = 45. Multiplying 30 by two-thirds (20) is the trap: using less per wash must give more washes.

text:
Using a phone while driving causes many crashes. After a crash, investigators can check the driver's phone records to see whether a call was in progress, but they cannot easily tell whether the driver was reading messages on the screen at the moment of impact. Such evidence is far less conclusive than, for example, a speed camera's record of a car's speed.
Which one of the following can be drawn as a conclusion of the passage above?
options: Using a phone causes more crashes than speeding.
It will be harder to prove that a driver was reading messages than that they were speeding.
The law should require phones to be switched off in cars.
Drivers who read messages are more careless than other drivers.
It is unfair to prosecute drivers for reading messages.
solution: The passage contrasts weak evidence of reading messages with the strong evidence of a speed camera, so proving message-reading will be harder. It does not compare the number of crashes from each cause, proposes no law, says nothing about drivers' general carelessness, and does not say prosecution would be unfair.

text: Which one of these did Leonardo da Vinci NOT do?
options: paint The Last Supper in Milan
paint the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel
make detailed anatomical drawings of the human body
solution: The Sistine Chapel ceiling was painted by Michelangelo between 1508 and 1512. Leonardo painted the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, filled notebooks with inventions such as flying machines, and dissected bodies for his anatomical drawings.

text:
A piece of cheese normally costs €4.50. This week it is labelled "€0.50 off". The shop also offers 20% off the whole bill when you spend €20 or more.
If I spend more than €20 in total, how much does the cheese cost me?
solution: The €0.50 comes off first, giving €4.00 on the bill; the 20% discount then applies to the whole bill, including that €4.00: €4.00 x 0.8 = €3.20. Taking 20% off €4.50 and then subtracting €0.50 gives €3.10, which treats the offers in the wrong order.

text:
A study of adopted children found that their musical ability resembled that of their biological parents more closely than that of the parents who raised them. Many people find this discouraging, as if talent were handed out at birth. Yet music teachers have always noticed that some children pick up an instrument far faster than others from their very first lesson. Whether we call this a gift or put it down to genes, children clearly do not all start from the same place.
Which one of the following statements is best supported as the conclusion of the passage?
options: Practice makes no difference to musical skill.
Music teachers can tell which children will become professional musicians.
Adopted children should be taught music by their biological parents.
We may as well accept that people begin with different levels of musical aptitude.
solution: The passage argues that, whatever the explanation, children start with different aptitudes, and that this need not discourage us. It does not say ability is entirely inherited, that practice is useless, that teachers can predict careers, or that biological parents should teach.

text:
Two bus companies run along the same road from town A to town B, at steady speeds. Company X buses leave A every 15 minutes and take 60 minutes to reach B. Company Y buses leave A every 10 minutes and take 36 minutes.
A Company Y driver leaves A 5 minutes after the previous X bus has left.
How many X buses travelling from A to B does she overtake before she reaches B?
solution: Measure time from the departure of the X bus just before her, so she leaves at 5 and arrives at 41. She catches the X bus that left at 0 when (t - 5)/36 = t/60, at t = 12.5. The one that left at -15 is caught when (t - 5)/36 = (t + 15)/60, at t = 35, while it is still on the road (it arrives at 45). The one that left at -30 arrives at B at 30, before she can reach it. So she overtakes 2.

text:
After five days a cyclist has completed 40% of a long-distance route. Over the next three days she plans to cover half of the distance that then remains, which will leave her 90 km to ride on the final two days.
How long is the route?
solution: After 40%, 60% of the route remains. Half of that, 30% of the route, is covered in the next three days, leaving the final 30%, which is 90 km. So the route is 90 / 0.3 = 300 km.

text:
A closed wooden chest measures 60 cm wide, 40 cm deep and 30 cm high on the outside. The lid and the four sides are made of wood 2 cm thick, but the base is 5 cm thick.
What is the inside height of the chest?
solution: The inside height is the outside height minus the lid and the base: 30 - 2 - 5 = 23 cm. The sides do not affect the height. 26 cm wrongly treats the base as 2 cm thick, and 25 cm forgets the lid.

text:
The tables show economic growth and inflation for five countries in two quarters of a year.

| economic growth (%) | first quarter | second quarter |
|---|---|---|
| Spain | 0.5 | 0.7 |
| Italy | 0.2 | 0.2 |
| Poland | 0.9 | 0.8 |
| Sweden | 0.3 | 0.6 |
| Austria | 0.4 | 0.3 |

| inflation (%) | first quarter | second quarter |
|---|---|---|
| Spain | 2.1 | 2.4 |
| Italy | 1.5 | 1.2 |
| Poland | 3.0 | 2.6 |
| Sweden | 1.8 | 1.6 |
| Austria | 2.0 | 2.0 |

A report comparing the second quarter with the first says: "Growth has picked up, while inflation has eased."
Which country is the report describing?
solution: Growth rose only in Spain and Sweden. Of those two, inflation fell in Sweden (1.8 to 1.6) but rose in Spain (2.1 to 2.4). Italy and Poland had falling inflation but no rise in growth, and Austria's inflation did not change.

text: What does a ribosome make directly when it translates an mRNA molecule?
options: a folded enzyme made of several chains
a DNA copy of the gene
solution: Translation joins amino acids in the order set by the codons, making a polypeptide chain: the primary structure. Folding into the final 3-D shape, and joining with other chains, happens afterwards and is not the direct product. mRNA comes from transcription.

text: Which one of the following lies in the thorax, ABOVE the diaphragm, in a human?
solution: The diaphragm separates the thorax (heart, lungs, thymus, the lower trachea) from the abdomen. The thymus sits in front of the heart, in the chest. The stomach, spleen, kidneys and pancreas are all abdominal organs below the diaphragm.

text: Which one of the following contains NO nucleotides?
solution: Cellulose is a polysaccharide of glucose. Ribosomes contain rRNA, chromosomes contain DNA, every virus has DNA or RNA, and ATP is itself a nucleotide (adenine, ribose and three phosphates).

text: Which statement about mitochondria is NOT correct?
options: Mitochondria are the site of the Krebs cycle.
solution: Glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm; only its product, pyruvate, enters the mitochondrion. Everything else is true: two membranes (the inner one folded into cristae), a small circular DNA, their own small ribosomes, and the Krebs cycle in the matrix.

text:
One strand of a short piece of DNA reads TGC-CAT-AGG.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1 The other strand includes the triplet ACG.
2 Each of the three triplets is held to the other strand by 8 hydrogen bonds.
3 If this strand is the template, the mRNA made from it contains 2 uracil bases.
solution: 1: TGC pairs with ACG. 2: A-T pairs have 2 hydrogen bonds and G-C pairs 3. TGC has 2 + 3 + 3 = 8, but CAT has 3 + 2 + 2 = 7, so not all three have 8. 3: the mRNA is ACG-GUA-UCC, with 2 uracils. So 1 and 3 only.

text: Which one of the following is NOT part of the body's defence against pathogens?
options: mucus and cilia in the trachea
solution: Red blood cells carry oxygen and have no defensive role. Mucus traps microbes and cilia sweep them away, stomach acid kills many that are swallowed, lysozyme breaks down bacterial walls, and a clot seals a wound so pathogens cannot get in.

text:
In which stages of aerobic respiration is reduced NAD produced?
1 glycolysis
2 the link reaction
3 the Krebs cycle
4 oxidative phosphorylation
solution: NAD is reduced in glycolysis, in the link reaction (pyruvate to acetyl coenzyme A) and several times in the Krebs cycle. Oxidative phosphorylation does the opposite: it oxidises reduced NAD back to \(\mathrm{NAD^+}\), passing its electrons along the chain to oxygen.

text:
In a sample of double-stranded DNA, 21% of the bases are adenine.
What percentage of the bases are cytosine?
solution: A pairs with T, so thymine is also 21%, and A + T = 42%. The remaining 58% is G + C, split equally because G pairs with C: cytosine is 29%. 58 is G and C together.

text: Which stage of mitosis comes immediately BEFORE anaphase?
solution: The order is prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, followed by cytokinesis; interphase comes between divisions. Metaphase, when the chromosomes line up at the equator, comes just before anaphase, when the chromatids are pulled apart.

text:
The frequency of an allele in a small population of beetles changes over several generations.
Which of the following could cause this?
1 genetic drift
2 natural selection
3 beetles from another population moving in and breeding
solution: Allele frequencies change by chance (genetic drift, strongest in small populations), when some alleles help survival and reproduction (natural selection), and when individuals bring in alleles from elsewhere (gene flow by migration). All three.

text: Which molecule is USED UP in photosynthesis and PRODUCED by aerobic respiration?
solution: Photosynthesis fixes carbon dioxide into sugar, and respiration releases it again. Oxygen and glucose go the other way round: made in photosynthesis, used in respiration. Reduced NADP belongs to photosynthesis only, and chlorophyll is not used up.

text:
A plant cell is seen in metaphase of mitosis.
Which of these features could be used, at this moment, to show that it is eukaryotic rather than prokaryotic?
1 a cell wall
2 chloroplasts
3 a nuclear envelope
solution: Chloroplasts are membrane-bound organelles, found only in eukaryotes. Many prokaryotes also have a cell wall, so a wall proves nothing. And during metaphase the nuclear envelope has broken down, so it cannot be seen. 2 only.

chapter: States of Matter and Gas Laws
text: Which statement about changes of state is NOT correct?
options: Melting absorbs energy from the surroundings.
Condensation releases energy to the surroundings.
Sublimation is a solid turning directly into a gas.
The boiling point of a liquid depends on the surrounding pressure.
Evaporation can only happen at the boiling point.
solution: Evaporation happens from a liquid's surface at any temperature (puddles dry at 20 °C); boiling is evaporation throughout the liquid, at the temperature where vapour pressure equals the surrounding pressure. The other statements are correct.

text:
Ethanal can be made from ethene in three steps:
\[\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} \xrightarrow{1\ (\mathrm{HBr})} \mathrm{CH_3CH_2Br} \xrightarrow{2\ (\mathrm{NaOH(aq)})} \mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} \xrightarrow{3\ (\mathrm{acidified\ K_2Cr_2O_7})} \mathrm{CH_3CHO}\]
Which types of reaction are steps 1, 2 and 3?
solution: 1: HBr adds across the C=C double bond (addition). 2: hydroxide replaces the bromine (nucleophilic substitution). 3: dichromate removes hydrogen from the alcohol, turning it into an aldehyde (oxidation).

text:
Which of the following must be true of two compounds in the same homologous series?
1 They fit the same general formula.
2 They have the same functional group.
3 They have the same boiling point.
solution: A homologous series shares a general formula (such as \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+1}OH}\) for alcohols) and a functional group, so its members have similar chemical properties. Each member adds a \(\mathrm{CH_2}\), so physical properties such as boiling point change steadily along the series. 1 and 2 only.

text:
Which of the following statements about the double bond in ethene is/are correct?
1 It is shorter than the C-C single bond in ethane.
2 It is made of one sigma bond and one pi bond.
3 It prevents rotation of one end of the molecule relative to the other.
solution: Four shared electrons pull the carbons closer, so C=C is shorter than C-C (1). The double bond is a sigma bond along the axis plus a pi bond above and below it (2). Twisting would break the sideways pi overlap, so rotation is restricted, which is why alkenes can have cis-trans isomers (3). All three.

text:
Here are some compounds of sulfur:
\(\mathrm{H_2S} \quad \mathrm{SO_2} \quad \mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3} \quad \mathrm{SO_3} \quad \mathrm{H_2SO_4}\)
Which list gives exactly the oxidation numbers shown by sulfur in these compounds? (In \(\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}\), take both sulfur atoms as equal.)

Potassium manganate(VII) oxidises concentrated hydrochloric acid to chlorine:
\[2\mathrm{KMnO_4} + a\,\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{KCl} + 2\mathrm{MnCl_2} + b\,\mathrm{Cl_2} + c\,\mathrm{H_2O}\]
What must \(c\) be for the equation to balance?
solution: Balance oxygen first: 2 \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) have 8 O, all ending in water, so \(c = 8\). Then hydrogen: 16 H in water means \(a = 16\). Chlorine: 16 on the left, and 2 (KCl) + 4 (\(\mathrm{MnCl_2}\)) = 6 on the right, leaving 10 Cl as 5 \(\mathrm{Cl_2}\). 16 is \(a\) and 5 is \(b\).

text:
How many oxygen atoms are in 88 g of carbon dioxide?
[Relative atomic masses: C = 12; O = 16; Avogadro constant = \(6.0 \times 10^{23}\ \mathrm{mol^{-1}}\)]
solution: \(M_r\) of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) = 44, so 88 g is 2.0 mol of molecules. Each has two O atoms: 4.0 mol of O atoms = \(4.0 \times 6.0 \times 10^{23} = 2.4 \times 10^{24}\). \(1.2 \times 10^{24}\) is the number of molecules.

subject: Physics
text:
A simple pendulum swings to and fro with a small amplitude.
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1 The bob moves fastest at the lowest point of its swing.
2 The bob's acceleration is zero at each end of its swing.
3 The bob's gravitational potential energy is greatest at each end of its swing.
solution: Energy moves between kinetic and potential: the bob is highest (most potential energy) at the ends and lowest, and fastest, in the middle. At the ends it stops for an instant, but the restoring force, and so the acceleration, is at its LARGEST there; acceleration is zero at the centre. 1 and 3 only.

subject: Mathematics
text: A circle has centre (2, -3) and radius 4. Which of the following is its equation?
solution: \((x - 2)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 16\) expands to \(x^2 - 4x + 4 + y^2 + 6y + 9 = 16\), so \(x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 6y - 3 = 0\). Wrong signs on \(4x\) and \(6y\) put the centre at (-2, 3), and forgetting the 4 + 9 gives the -16 version.

subject: Physics
text:
In these expressions, \(F\) = force, \(s\) = distance, \(m\) = mass, \(v\) = velocity, \(P\) = power, \(t\) = time, \(I\) = current and \(R\) = resistance.
Which of them have the unit of energy?
1 \(Fs\)
2 \(\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\)
3 \(\dfrac{P}{t}\)
4 \(I^2Rt\)
solution: Force x distance is work, in joules. \(\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\) is kinetic energy: kg m²/s² = J. \(I^2R\) is electrical power, so \(I^2Rt\) is energy. Power DIVIDED by time is J/s², not energy; power TIMES time would be.

subject: Mathematics
text:
Simplify
\[\log\frac{x^3}{2} + \log\frac{4}{x} - \log 2x\]
solution: Adding logs multiplies and subtracting divides: \(\log\left(\dfrac{x^3}{2} \times \dfrac{4}{x} \div 2x\right) = \log\dfrac{4x^3}{4x^2} = \log x\). A sum of logs is never the log of a sum.

subject: Mathematics
text: For which values of \(x\) are both \(x^2 - 9 < 0\) and \(3x - 2 \geq 4\) true?
solution: \(x^2 < 9\) means \(-3 < x < 3\) (strict, so 3 is excluded). \(3x \geq 6\) means \(x \geq 2\) (2 included). Both together: \(2 \leq x < 3\).
